item.title: Shika no Tsunokiri: Nara's Deer Antler-Cutting Ceremony — Guide
item.description: Shika no Tsunokiri (deer antler-cutting) is a traditional autumn ceremony held near Kasuga Taisha since the 17th century, when the sacred stags of Nara Park have their antlers safely removed before the rutting season. During autumn the bucks grow aggressive and their sharp antlers can injure people and other deer, so in this ritual — part animal management, part spectacle — Shinto-costumed handlers (seko) chase and catch a stag with ropes in a wooden arena, calm it, and a priest ceremonially saws off the antlers as an offering.
